whyItMatters: Disabled certificate verification lets any certificate pass, so an active attacker can intercept credentials, tokens, and response data crossing that HTTPS connection.
actions: Delete verify=False at the flagged call site and re-run the request against the real endpoint.
If the endpoint uses a private CA, pass the CA bundle path as the verify argument instead of disabling verification.
Search the codebase for other verify=False occurrences and remove them the same way.
verification: The finding disappears on rescan and requests succeed with default verification.
